Residue note from #13799 batch 8a (PR #15308, ACCEPT `5539256020`, Q1 ruled A): the red line now has two spellings across the b5 recipe — the four 8a files whose floor shares a COUNTED sink print `N failure(s) (cases and floor)` (the recipe's forward spelling, also recipe A's), while #15217's nine keep a plain case count on a red run. Not wrong, less precise; no back-port PR — the next b5 dispatch states the annotated spelling. Recorded here beside the 24 inline assertions so one card carries the recipe's residue.

Triage: lands in `domain:devx` (`scripts/check-agent-model-declared.mjs`, `check-startup-registry-verdict.mjs`, `js-comment-mask.mjs`); rationale: class (b) on the **over-claim**, under the line this seat applied today on objectui#8141 (admitted) versus objectui#8286 / #16207 (closed): a gate that runs and reports a verdict **broader than what it checked** is in class, because the absence hides behind a green. `Task` — the deliverable carries a decision.

⭐ **The over-claim is exact and is what makes this more than a follow-up note**: `measure-self-test-floor.mjs` reads **per file**, all three files now report **`ROSTER`**, and the 24 residual assertions are therefore invisible to *the very instrument that produced #13799's worklist*. ⇒ The defect that census exists to find — *"a green run registers nothing"* — is now sitting one level down, **under a floored file's name**. A file marked ROSTER reads as done; three of them are not.

The 24 are counted per file (4 + 8 + 12) with the block named in each case, and the mechanism is stated rather than assumed: each writes into the shared failure sink **only when it FAILS**, so deleting one leaves the run green and the verdict line unchanged. ⇒ Disappearance is indistinguishable from passing, which is the definition the floor recipe exists to defeat.

`priority:p3`: ⛔ **not a defect in any gate's judgement** — all 24 assertions pass today and none was touched by batch 7b. Nothing is wrong; what is missing is the guarantee that they still exist. And the exposure is bounded to three files.

⚠️ **The trap here is sharp and a fixer who misses it will reintroduce the exact defect being fixed.** For `js-comment-mask`'s `extra`, the rows exist **only because an `x(...)` call pushed them at runtime** ⇒ a roster **derived** from that loop would delete its own floor along with the call. That is precisely what recipe A exists to prevent. ⛔ Do not derive; each of the three blocks needs a **literal** roster of its own, in the shape pilot PR #15271 settled.

⇒ The alternative is a ruling rather than a patch, and it is legitimate: **decide that reach-only floors do not extend to inline assertions**, and say so where the recipe is written. ⚠️ If that is the answer, then `measure-self-test-floor.mjs`'s `ROSTER` verdict needs to say what it covers — otherwise the over-claim above survives the decision and this card returns under a different file's name.

⛔ This seat grades and routes only: not claimed, not dispatched, no code, and ⛔ it does not choose between the literal-roster route and the ruling.

Ruling: batch #198 item 5 · letter B · maintainer 「同意」 2026-09-20T12:03Z

Director seat, summon #25, `session_012GcsUbuqFGBibkEDMRC1eE`. Presented in detail with the recommendation **B** (fallback A); the maintainer agreed 「同意」. Thread re-read to its last comment (5570109892) in the act that wrote this.

## Ruling — B: recipe A's floor stops at the table rows, and the verdict says so

- The self-test floor discipline (recipe A, #13799 / pilot PR #15271) covers **table-driven rows only**. Inline assertions written below the driving loop are outside the floor; no literal roster is authored for the 24 residual assertions in `scripts/check-agent-model-declared.mjs` (4), `scripts/check-startup-registry-verdict.mjs` (8) and `scripts/js-comment-mask.mjs` (12).
- The boundary is written where the recipe is written (one sentence: reach-only floors do not extend to inline assertions), and **`scripts/measure-self-test-floor.mjs`'s `ROSTER` verdict states what it covers** (rows only), so the verdict line no longer claims a file's whole self-test is floored. That second half is the deliverable, ⛔ not optional: without it the over-claim survives the decision and the card returns under another file's name (triage's own condition at 5570109892).
- **A refused**: three literal rosters are three permanent obligations bought against zero measured harm (all 24 pass today, none touched by batch 7b), under the maintainer's principles 「不希望一直开发门禁」 and 「零拉动默认 defer 或 remove」.

Four-facet reading (this seat's own): ① B shrinks the contract to what it enforces, A adds three carriers; ② nobody is harmed — the pull is the over-claim itself, which B removes; ③ leans A (deleting an inline assertion stays silent after B) — the one facet against, outweighed; ④ remove beats declare-and-maintain.

`Prior rulings read: recipe, floors, table, rows, inline, assertions, roster → 87 term hits, 10 ADR decisions (ADR-0020 D1, ADR-0029 D9.7, ADR-0056 D10, ADR-0076 D11, ADR-0119 D3, ADR-0120 D2, ADR-0131 D1/D3/D7/D13) — all term-overlap on floor / roster in unrelated domains, none governs the self-test floor (the filing seat's check at card filing, control Decision 130 hits); #13799 (the discipline's parent card — a different question, ⛔ not merged with this ruling).`

Confidence gap carried: the 「a derived roster deletes its own floor」 reading for `js-comment-mask`'s `extra` was not reproduced by this seat; under B it is moot (no roster is written).

## Execution, same stroke

`needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue`. `tooling` · `priority:p3` · `domain:devx` untouched; type `Task` (the deliverable is the recipe sentence plus the verdict wording). Clause-②: no.
